key_insight: The local tangent residual (LTR) estimates whether nonlinear compression can outperform POD before training an autoencoder.
engineering_relevance: LTR can guide reduced-order modelling choices for turbulent flows, helping avoid costly autoencoder searches when POD is sufficient.
method: Estimate nonlinear compression potential from local data geometry using LTR, without model training or a threshold parameter.
Compare LTR trends with autoencoder compression performance.
Quantify trained-decoder nonlinearity using decoder linearisation error (DLE) relative to a linearised surrogate.
evidence_signal: Across two vortex street cases and a turbulent wind-turbine wake, LTR reproduced dominant autoencoder compression trends, with large nonlinear potential corroborated by large DLE.
watch_item: Validation covers three flow cases; generalisation to other turbulent regimes and datasets remains to be established.
paper_title: A Priori Estimation of the Non-Linear Compression Potential and Quantification of Autoencoder Non-Linearity in Turbulent Flows
